papers.title: Shape thinking and students' graphing activity
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 18th Annual Conference on Research in Undergraduate Mathematics Education (RUME)
papers.abstract: We describe a construct called shape thinking that characterizes individuals' ways of thinking about graphs. We introduce shape thinking in two forms—static and emergent—that have materialized in our work with students and teachers over the past two decades. Static shape thinking entails thinking of a graph as an object in and of itself, and as having properties that the student associates with learned facts. Emergent shape thinking entails envisioning a graph in terms of what is made (a trace) and how it is made (covarying quantities). We provide illustrations of the shape thinking forms using examples from data that we have gathered with secondary students, teachers, and undergraduate students.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Learners should construct/trace curves (emergent) rather than only match static cheatsheet shapes; supports interactive draw/pick-which-curve probes.

papers.title: Graphical shape thinking and transfer
papers.abstract: Updates the shape-thinking stem phrase to graphical shape thinking. Emergent graphical shape thinking characterizes a student's actions that involve conceiving a graph simultaneously in terms of what is made (a trace entailing corresponding values) and how it is made (a sustained image of quantities having covaried).
papers.pedagogy_implication: Big-O teach should treat growth curves as traces of ops vs n, not decorative icons.

papers.title: Visualizing Algorithm Analysis Topics
papers.abstract: We have devised an approach that we term Algorithm Analysis Visualizations (AAVs), capable of conveying AA concepts visually. In AAVs, analysis is presented as a series of slides where each statement of the explanation is connected to visuals that support the sentence. Evaluation across CS3114 offerings found intervention students spent more time with material and performed better on the AA part of the final exam.
papers.pedagogy_implication: OpenDSA-style growth-rate visuals beat prose-only algorithm analysis.

papers.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Algorithm Analysis Visualizations
papers.abstract: We developed visualizations named Algorithm Analysis Visualizations (AAVs) that focus on conveying algorithm analysis concepts. Results indicate intervention students spent significantly more time with AAVs than control students who used primarily textual content, gave positive feedback, and had better performance on the analysis part of the final exam.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Cite for multi-curve / growth-rate teach frames in Study-os Big O lessons.

papers.title: Role of Lines and Points in the Construction of Emergent Graphical Shape Thinking
papers.abstract: Reports on a student who demonstrated evidence of early elements of emergent shape thinking (representing quantities on axes; forming a multiplicative object) but showed contraindication of assimilating a graph as an emergent record due to meanings for points and lines.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Interactive plot probes must check point/line meanings, not only final shape match.

papers.title: Designing task sequences to support emergent graphical shape thinking (6th grade)
papers.abstract: Describes design of a task sequence supporting 6th-grade students in developing emergent graphical shape thinking (EGST): conceiving a graph as a record of covarying quantities that can be created by imagining the trace of a multiplicative object.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Catalog-wide pipeline should sequence construct-then-check graph tasks.

papers.title: Identifying static- and emergent-shape thinking in students' language about graphs of functions
papers.abstract: Analyzes students' language for static-shape vs emergent-shape thinking (Moore & Thompson, 2015). Static thinking treats graphs as inherent shapes independent of scales; emergent thinking treats graphs as traces of covarying quantities.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Typed review / probe prompts can elicit shape-thinking language.

papers.title: The number line is a critical spatial-numerical representation: Evidence from a fraction intervention
papers.abstract: Using a pretest-training-posttest design, we examined second and third graders' fraction learning in 3 conditions: number line training, area model training, and a non-numerical control. Children who received number line training improved at representing fractions with number lines, and children who received area model training improved at representing fractions with area models. Critically, only the number line training led to transfer to an untrained fraction magnitude comparison task. We conclude that the number line plays a causal role in children's fraction magnitude understanding, and is more beneficial than the widely used area model.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Fractions teach/explain/worked must be number-line-first; area models are secondary.

papers.title: Fraction Intervention for Students With Mathematics Difficulties: Lessons Learned From Five Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.abstract: Across five RCTs, intervention students significantly outperformed controls on number line estimation of fractions (mean ES 0.93). Performance on the number line task is a strong predictor of fraction learning across Grades 3–5 and more advanced mathematics achievement, including algebra.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Number-line estimation is the primary outcome visual for fractions interventions.

papers.title: An integrated theory of whole number and fractions development (ERIC deposit)
papers.abstract: Integrated theory proposing that fractions are understood as magnitudes on a mental number line; number-line estimation accuracy predicts later math achievement.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Aligns Study-os fraction visuals with magnitude-on-line representation.

papers.title: IES REL Teaching Fractions Toolkit (Module 1 materials)
papers.abstract: US ED / IES practice materials emphasizing fraction magnitude on the number line for classroom professional learning (Module 1).
papers.pedagogy_implication: Government PD source for number-line-first fraction teach frames (public domain US gov).

papers.title: OpenDSA Comparing Algorithms / growth rates module
papers.abstract: OpenDSA module showing a graph for six equations illustrating growth rates and a table of relative growth rates for representative input sizes. Used as the course growth-rate plot family referenced by issue #161.
papers.pedagogy_implication: Source family for multi-curve growth charts; Study-os teach subset uses only O(1)/log n/n/n².
